options.configurable_policy: Resolve policy for new capsules, record it in receipts, and preserve historic values; current API deliberately exposes no override.

default_256_kib_simulation.note: Transient policy simulation inside this analysis process only. No source/config edits, model calls, publication, or persisted candidate/receipt changes.

compatibility_correction: A default increase follows the existing ceiling-increase compatibility design when old supported ceilings remain accepted. Three actual stored 192 KiB capsules remained intact and byte-identical in the transient 256 KiB simulation. Existing repository tests separately cover the legacy 64 KiB ceiling. No persisted receipt or source code was modified.

model_capacity_input.source: Owner reports the base models in use have a 1,000,000-token context window
model_capacity_input.note: Owner-provided capacity; this investigation does not equate byte counts with token counts or independently benchmark provider limits.

recommendation.primary: Replace the low fixed canonical byte ceiling with an explicit larger configurable budget for new contexts, plus a separate check of the full rendered prompt against the selected model token window with output/reasoning/harness reserve. Preserve all historical recorded ceilings and exact receipts.
recommendation.short_term: A compatible 256 KiB default clears the current refusal, but it is an interim unblock rather than a long-term sizing policy for 1M-token models.
recommendation.efficiency: Lossless relation-node interning saves 25418 bytes in this case and clears the current cap, but requires a versioned representation and readability/replay tests. Shared prose is already deduplicated.
recommendation.prose_scope: A narrower feedback row still exceeds the cap. A dedicated prose-only context could improve efficiency, but requires an enforced operation capability and exact owner/span coverage; it is more work than a budget policy change.
